reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it guides viewers to register for and fund a branded trading account by providing identity information and sending Bitcoin, then submitting payment proof. It associates confirmed funding with paid-member status and trading bonuses or results, making the video's own financial solicitation return-related. The material does not establish actual deposits, withdrawals, losses, or the service's legitimacy.

citations.quote: Adding funds to your Meritrading International pool account.
Each day you will receive a statement via email telling you the results of the trades.
How to Register and Fund your Mirror Trading International Account
upload your proof of identity

opening.argument: Judge, the video asks viewers to read and accept terms and conditions before registering. It describes daily statements as reporting the results of trades, not as promising a fixed or guaranteed return. Even after Bitcoin is sent, the narration makes the account display conditional on an administrator confirming the transfer. Those distinctions matter: the material explains a process, but its cited language does not establish that any particular return is assured.

citations.quote: read the terms and conditions and then click I have read and accepted the terms and conditions
Once the admin has confirmed your Bitcoin transfer, it will appear in your trading account.
Each day you will receive a statement via email telling you the results of the trades.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution correctly identifies instructions to upload identity proof and fund an account. But those steps do not, by themselves, establish deceptive handling of either. Its statement citation says viewers will receive trade results; it does not quote a guaranteed profit. The title likewise identifies an account tutorial, not a promised rate of return. The case should turn on what this video actually claims, not on an outcome it does not show.

citations.quote: upload your proof of identity
Each day you will receive a statement via email telling you the results of the trades.
How to Register and Fund your Mirror Trading International Account

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Accepting unspecified terms is not a risk warning, and the absence of a quoted guarantee does not make the solicitation innocuous. The video instructs viewers to send Bitcoin to fund a pool account, then connects that funded account to daily trading results. Those are the concrete financial steps the defense's uncertainty argument leaves intact.

citations.quote: Adding funds to your Meritrading International pool account.
Make the payment by sending the bitcoin
Each day you will receive a statement via email telling you the results of the trades.

opening.argument: Judge, the organizing purpose is operational instruction. The title calls this a guide to registering and funding an account; the narration walks through sponsor information, username availability, registration confirmation, a profile update, and how to view a daily statement. It tells the viewer where controls are and what information the interface requests. Showing the funding screen within that sequence does not establish that the demonstrated account will produce real profits or that the speaker is making such a promise.

citations.quote: How to Register and Fund your Mirror Trading International Account
The system will tell you if the username is available
a screen will come up with a confirmation message which will confirm your login details.
Click the view option to see your daily statement.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution reads the Bitcoin and identity steps as solicitation, but its evidence also fits an account walkthrough: the narration directs viewers through registration, profile setup, payment entry, and statement viewing. A tutorial can explain a funding procedure without proving that funds were received or that reported results were realized. The cited screenshot of the profile page establishes a requested identity field, not what happens to submitted documents.

citations.quote: Please update your personal details and upload your proof of identity.
Fill in the details. The exact amount of Bitcoin you sent. Enter the blockchain transaction ID or TX ID. Upload the proof of payment screenshot. Then click submit.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The instructional format is precisely how the video moves a viewer toward funding. It does not merely describe an interface: it tells the viewer to send Bitcoin, submit transaction details and payment proof, and expect trading results afterward. A lack of demonstrated profits does not erase that account-funding solicitation.

citations.quote: Make the payment by sending the bitcoin
Enter the blockchain transaction ID or TX ID. Upload the proof of payment screenshot. Then click submit.
Each day you will receive a statement via email telling you the results of the trades.

opening.argument: Judge, the observable transaction is an account-service workflow: register, supply profile details, send Bitcoin, and submit a transaction ID so the payment can be matched to the account. The narration also mentions sharing a registration link, but it does not state a commission rate or promise income for recruiting anyone. Nor does it promise a guaranteed trading return or show that a withdrawal was refused. Those missing claims matter when distinguishing a documented account-funding process from a demonstrated deceptive scheme.

citations.quote: Please update your personal details and upload your proof of identity.

Should you wish to refer your friends, you can send them your registration link

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's central point, that this is a pool account funded with Bitcoin, is supported. But funding alone does not show misappropriation, and a daily results statement does not establish a guaranteed payout. The paid-member display follows confirmation of a transfer; it is not, by itself, evidence that recruiting others pays or that the account's displayed results can or cannot be withdrawn.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing withdrawal or commission proof limits what can be concluded about outcomes, but it does not turn this into ordinary commerce. The video directs a viewer to send Bitcoin into a trading pool account, ties confirmation to paid-member status, and presents daily trade results as the reason to monitor that account. The defense acknowledges the central funding mechanism while treating the absence of later evidence as decisive.
